claims.claim: Reasoning models achieve strictly better verbalized-confidence calibration than non-reasoning counterparts in 33 of 36 settings.
claims.scope_conditions: TriviaQA, NonambigQA, SuperGPQA and MMLU-Pro subsets; no code
claims.quoted_support: they achieve strictly better confidence calibration than their non-reasoning counterparts in 33 out of the 36 settings.

breadth.model_families_and_sizes: Qwen2.5-32B-based (R1-Distill-Qwen, OR1-Preview, QwQ), GLM-4/Z1-0414 32B, EXAONE-3.5/Deep, Qwen3 (Sec 3.1)
breadth.base_vs_instruct: reasoning vs instruct pairs; no base models
breadth.reasoning_models: yes, reasoning enabled/disabled for Qwen3 via empty think block (Sec 3.1 footnote 3)
breadth.elicitation_formats: single verbalized-confidence prompt; slow-thinking ICL variant (Sec 4-5)
breadth.benchmarks: TriviaQA, NonambigQA, SuperGPQA subset, MMLU-Pro subset (Table 1)
breadth.granularity: whole answer; confidence along CoT steps (Sec 5)
breadth.causal_intervention: removal/insertion of slow-thinking behaviors in CoT (Sec 5), not hidden-state

claims.claim: Calibration gains are not a byproduct of accuracy: GLM-Z1-0414 has 0.07 lower accuracy than GLM-4-0414 on NonambigQA yet 0.037 lower ECE and 0.078 higher AUROC.
claims.quoted_support: Notably, reasoning models exhibit superior calibration even in cases where they underperform non-reasoning models in task accuracy.

claims.claim: Calibration improves progressively along the CoT for reasoning models, and removing slow-thinking behaviors degrades it.
claims.quoted_support: reasoning models become increasingly better calibrated as their CoT unfolds, a trend not observed in non-reasoning models. Moreover, removing slow thinking behaviors from the CoT leads to a significant drop in calibration.
